newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: INTERVIEW-LITHUANIA AIMS FOR BALANCED BUDGET, TAXES KEY.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-LITHUANIA AIMS FOR BALANCED BUDGET, TAXES KEY.

text.p: Lithuanian Finance Minister Algirdas Shemeta says the government is aiming for a balanced budget by the year 2000 and says getting tax collection on track will be the key to this objective.
"We expect growth on the revenue side by significantly improving tax organisation," Shemeta told Reuters in an interview.
"Recently we approved a comprehensive programm on tax administration improvement," he said.
The programme in started March and Shemeta claimed the results were already evident.
"Revenues in April were 50 percent higher than in December last year," Shemeta said. "December is usually one of the best months for tax collection."
Compared to last April revenues were "even higher" this year, Shemeta said.
"For the first time in several years, we fulfilled the revenue collection plan for four months and are already in a little surplus," Shemeta said.
"Having in mind the sharp decrease in revenues in January and February, it's a very positive trend in revenue collection," he said.
Reducing the number of exemptions is another central plank in the government's plans to put its fiscal house in order and reduce its debt load.

"The first wave of reducing exemptions was made in March this year, when we actually equalised the treatment of foreign and domestic businesses in company tax," Shemeta said. "Companies are treated equally."
